definitions.explanation: The traditional lunisolar calendar used in Japan before the adoption of the Gregorian calendar in 1873. Still referenced for traditional festivals and seasonal events.

examples.japanese: {旧暦|きゅうれき}の{正月|しょうがつ}は2{月|がつ}ごろだ。
examples.english: New Year on the lunar calendar falls around February.

examples.japanese: {七夕|たなばた}は{旧暦|きゅうれき}では8{月|がつ}に{当|あ}たる。
examples.english: Tanabata falls in August on the lunar calendar.

examples.japanese: {沖縄|おきなわ}では{今|いま}でも{旧暦|きゅうれき}に{基|もと}づいて{行事|ぎょうじ}を{行|おこな}う{地域|ちいき}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In Okinawa, many areas still hold events based on the lunar calendar.

notes:
USAGE:
Japan adopted the Gregorian calendar ({新暦|しんれき}) in 1873 (Meiji 6). The old lunisolar calendar is still called {旧暦|きゅうれき} and remains relevant for traditional festivals, especially in Okinawa and rural areas. Some seasonal events ({お{盆|ぼん}}, {七夕|たなばた}) are celebrated on either the old or new calendar depending on the region.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旧暦|きゅうれき}の{正月|しょうがつ}: New Year by the lunar calendar
- {旧暦|きゅうれき}に{基|もと}づく: based on the lunar calendar
- {旧暦|きゅうれき}で{言|い}うと: in terms of the lunar calendar

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新暦|しんれき}: new calendar (Gregorian calendar)
- {太陰暦|たいいんれき}: lunar calendar (technical term)
- {暦|こよみ}: calendar (general)
